name: Question 8
problem: In what direction does the function $f(x,y)=x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+y{e}^{x}-xy$ increase most rapidly at the point $(-1,1)?$
worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $f(x,y)$ increases most rapidly in the direction of its gradient at that point.

So, we compute $∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(-1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+y{e}^{x}-xy)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+y{e}^{x}-xy)\text{ }j \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡y+y{e}^{x}-y)\text{ }i+(\frac{x}{y}+{e}^{x}-x)\text{ }j \\ ∇f(1,1) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡1+1\cdot {e}^{-1}-1)\text{ }i+(\frac{-1}{1}+{e}^{-1}-(-1))\text{ }j \\  & =({e}^{-1}-1)\text{ }i+{e}^{-1}j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the function increases most rapidly in the direction of $({e}^{-1}-1)\text{ }i+{e}^{-1}j.$

Question 8
?

In what direction does the function f(x,y)=xln⁡y+yex−xy increase most rapidly at the point (−1,1)?

a
(e−1+1) i+(e−1−1)j
b
(e−1−1) i+e−1j
c
(e−1) i+ej
d
(e−1+1) i+e−1j
e
(e+1) i+(e−1)j
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

At a given point, a function f(x,y) increases most rapidly in the direction of its gradient at that point.

So, we compute ∇f(x,y) and evaluate it at the point (−1,1):

∇f(x,y)=∂∂x(xln⁡y+yex−xy) i+∂∂y(xln⁡y+yex−xy) j=(ln⁡y+yex−y) i+(xy+ex−x) j∇f(1,1)=(ln⁡1+1⋅e−1−1) i+(−11+e−1−(−1)) j=(e−1−1) i+e−1j

Therefore, the function increases most rapidly in the direction of (e−1−1) i+e−1j.
